neighbours.label: 'likely to' when a degree word grades it: 'more / less / far less / most / twice as likely to <verb>' about who does something (peaks on ' to'); quiet on plain 'is likely to' with no degree word, on 'most likely' used as an adverb ('will most likely close'), on 'the more likely outcome', and on 'more prone / apt / inclined / liable to'
fire: Teenagers who sleep less are more likely to skip breakfast.
Drivers over seventy are far less likely to speed than younger drivers.
Smokers were twice as likely to develop the disease in the study.
Of all the groups surveyed, retirees were the most likely to vote by mail.
Children with older siblings are less likely to be shy at school.
Customers who receive a reminder email are much more likely to renew their subscription.
In the trial, patients on the new drug were three times as likely to recover within a week.
Cats raised indoors are less likely to catch infections.
quiet: Teenagers who sleep less are likely to skip breakfast.
Drivers over seventy are far less prone to speed than younger drivers.
The store will most likely close early on Friday.
Of all the scenarios, a rainy weekend is the more likely outcome.
Children with older siblings are less inclined to be shy at school.
Customers who receive a reminder email are likely to renew their subscription.
In the trial, the new drug will most likely be approved next year.
Cats raised indoors are less liable to catch infections.
neighbours.notes: Test sentences written blind by a second author who saw only the label. Probes: 'more/less/most/twice as likely to' 0.61-1.02 peaking on ' to'; plain 'likely to' 0.10-0.17; 'more likely than' 0.16-0.36; 'most likely' adverb, 'likely that', probable/possible, prone/apt/inclined/liable ~0. Also fires strongly on Japanese 可能 after a verb-noun (実現可能, 三分割可能, 使用可能 in corpus context, 0.6-1.1) but not on a short '使用可能です' sentence; not tested here. Found via the resident feeders tool (attribution), since play step ran out of GPU memory. The solver (differential evolution) found no leak.
